sector_model: aircraft and engine lessor (financial/asset-heavy): book equity, debt to equity, interest coverage, fleet value, gains on sale, maintenance reserve revenue; FCF not meaningful because equipment purchases are the growth business
thesis: Willis Lease Finance (aircraft engine lessor) trades at 46.86 (2026-11-06 close), market cap about 992M on 21,162,209 shares (cover, 2026-10-30): about 14.0x TTM common earnings (TTM net income to common about 73.4M, diluted EPS about 3.35 split-adjusted) and about 1.36x WLFC book equity of 729.5M. Nine-month 2026 revenue rose 18.3% to 634.7M and operating cash flow rose to 239.0M, but nine-month net income fell 34% to 67.1M (diluted EPS 2.86 vs 4.63) and Q3 EPS fell to 0.47 from 1.08 as maintenance reserve revenue halved (39.3M vs 76.1M). Gross debt principal is 2.554B against 732.6M total equity (3.5x), and 15,000 redeemable preferred shares (98.0M carrying value) rank ahead of common.
counterthesis: Earnings are falling while the balance sheet is expanding: nine-month equipment purchases were 837.6M against 418.0M of sale proceeds and 239.0M operating cash flow, so net investment (about 420M) is funded by debt, preferred stock (5,250 new preferred shares in 2026, a further 8.09% Series B with DBJ) and the 2026 share split-adjusted share base. Q3 revenue growth came from 98.1M of spare parts and equipment sales (5.4M a year earlier), a low-margin and lumpy line, while core maintenance reserve revenue and gains on sale (5.5M vs 16.1M) fell. Related-party sales to funds it manages (216.2M of engines to the BXCI Fund with a 33.3M gain, 104.0M of notes to the LMI Fund) support earnings, and fair value of those transactions was not examined. Interest expense is about 127M a year TTM, covenant headroom is not quantified, 2028 and 2029 maturities are 256M and 266M, and floating-rate exposure was not read. Aviation cycle, lessee credit and engine residual values are the main risks.
invalidation: Q4 and Q1 net income to common continuing below prior-year levels; gains on sale and maintenance reserve revenue not recovering; debt to equity rising above about 4x or covenant waivers; preferred issuance rather than retained earnings funding growth; related-party fund sales slowing so that asset sales stop clearing; engine value impairments.
